subject: community-medicine
title: Blindness Control: NPCBVI, Cataract Backlog and Vision 2020

steps.title: Standard definitions of blindness and visual impairment
steps.tx: To align national standards with the World Health Organization, India modified its statutory **definition of blindness** to visual acuity of less than three-sixtieths in the better eye with best possible correction, or constriction of the visual field to less than ten degrees around central fixation. Visual acuity between six-eighteen and six-sixtieths denotes moderate visual impairment, while less than six-sixtieths down to three-sixtieths reflects severe visual impairment.
steps.say: Blindness is defined as vision worse than three over sixty in the better eye with glasses, or visual field under ten degrees. Vision between six-eighteen and six-sixtieths is visual impairment.

steps.title: National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment
steps.tx: Launched as a fully centrally sponsored scheme, the **NPCBVI program framework** coordinates public ophthalmic infrastructure across all Indian states and union territories. The programme focuses on decentralised eye care by upgrading primary health centres with vision centres, training ophthalmic assistants, conducting mobile eye screening in remote villages, providing free spectacles to poor schoolchildren, and reimbursing non-governmental hospitals performing high-volume charitable cataract surgeries.
steps.say: The National Programme for Control of Blindness establishes vision centres at primary clinics, conducts village eye screening camps, and provides free cataract surgeries and spectacles.

rows: High-volume IOL cataract surgery, glaucoma care

steps.title: Clearing the immense cataract backlog
steps.tx: Senile cataract accounts for approximately sixty-six percent of all avoidable blindness in India, creating a formidable **cataract backlog clearance** challenge for public health authorities. Clearing this accumulation requires performing over six to seven million intraocular lens surgeries annually, transitioning completely from outdated intracapsular cataract extraction to modern sutureless manual small incision cataract surgery (SICS) and phacoemulsification with posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation.
steps.say: Cataracts cause two-thirds of avoidable blindness in India. Clearing the backlog requires seven million surgeries each year using modern small-incision techniques with artificial lens implants.

steps.title: Surgical techniques: manual SICS versus phacoemulsification
steps.tx: In community eye camps, **manual small incision cataract surgery** represents the most cost-effective and dependable high-volume surgical technique. The surgeon constructs a self-sealing sclero-corneal tunnel, expresses the intact cataractous nucleus hydrodynamically without sutures, and inserts a rigid polymethylmethacrylate intraocular lens into the capsular bag, achieving rapid visual rehabilitation equivalent to expensive ultrasonic phacoemulsification at a fraction of the cost.
steps.say: Manual small incision cataract surgery delivers excellent visual recovery at low cost in high-volume camps. The surgeon removes the clouded lens through a self-sealing tunnel and inserts an artificial lens.

steps.title: Uncorrected refractive errors and school eye screening
steps.tx: The second leading cause of visual impairment across India is **uncorrected refractive error**, particularly uncorrected myopia in growing schoolchildren and presbyopia in working adults. To prevent amblyopia and scholastic failure, the national programme mandates annual school eye screening, where trained primary schoolteachers test visual acuity using Snellen charts, referring children failing the six-nine line to optometrists for free prescription spectacles.
steps.say: Uncorrected refractive errors blur vision for millions of schoolchildren and adults. Annual vision screening by schoolteachers identifies children needing glasses, providing spectacles free of charge.

nodes.label: Primary schoolteacher screens with Snellen chart

steps.title: Corneal blindness, trachoma and vitamin A
steps.tx: Excluding cataract and refractive error, **corneal blindness causes** account for nearly one percent of blindness, primarily resulting from childhood xerophthalmia due to vitamin A deficiency, ophthalmia neonatorum, infectious bacterial and fungal corneal ulcers, and historical trachoma scarring. Community prevention combines routine biannual vitamin A prophylaxis in preschool children with promoting the five clean practices during delivery to eliminate gonococcal eye contamination in newborns.
steps.say: Corneal blindness arises from childhood vitamin A deficiency, eye ulcers, birth infections and trachoma scarring. Routine vitamin A syrup and clean childbirth practices prevent corneal loss.

steps.title: Vision 2020: The Right to Sight global initiative
steps.tx: India joined the international coalition **Vision 2020 initiative**, a collaborative global campaign launched by the World Health Organization and the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness to eliminate avoidable blindness by the year 2020. The strategy established disease-specific targets, integrated comprehensive eye care into universal primary healthcare networks, strengthened national human resources for health, and expanded equitable rural eye hospital infrastructure.
steps.say: The Vision 2020 Right to Sight campaign was launched to eliminate avoidable blindness. It built rural eye care networks, trained eye surgeons and integrated eye health into general clinics.

steps.title: Rapid assessment of avoidable blindness surveys
steps.tx: To measure blindness prevalence and evaluate cataract surgical coverage without conducting costly whole-population censuses, epidemiologists conduct **rapid assessment of avoidable blindness** surveys. Using standardized cluster sampling of adults aged fifty years and older, field teams examine fifty clusters of fifty individuals using portable torches and pinholes, recording visual acuity and pinpointing barriers that prevent elderly villagers from accessing surgical care.
steps.say: Rapid assessment surveys screen adults aged fifty and older in sampled village clusters. The survey accurately measures blindness rates and identifies why villagers have not had cataract surgery.

steps.title: Hospital corneal retrieval and eye donation
steps.tx: Restoring vision to individuals with corneal scarring requires expanding **hospital cornea retrieval programs**, operating through certified community eye banks and grief counsellors stationed in hospital trauma centers. Corneal tissue must be harvested within six hours of death under aseptic conditions using whole-globe enucleation or in-situ corneoscleral button excision, followed by storage in McCarey-Kaufman or Optisol medium for lamellar or penetrating keratoplasty.
steps.say: Eye banks rely on hospital retrieval programmes where grief counsellors support families with donation. Donated corneas must be retrieved within six hours of death to restore sight.
